programme: AHR acts as the sensor of smoke-derived aryl-hydrocarbon carcinogens (its target list itself contains the canonical detox genes CYP1A1, CYP1B1, ALDH3A1, plus its own ARNT dimerisation partner). SIM2, a second ARNT-partnering bHLH-PAS factor whose targets include ARNT and HIF1A, sits in the same structural family and links the response to hypoxia/apoptosis (BCL2, CASP3). BTG2 carries the downstream antioxidant buffering arm (targets SOD1, SOD2, CAT) that a sustained AHR-driven oxidative load would recruit. MXI1, the MYC-restraining member of the MAX network (targets MYC, MYCN, CCNB1, ODC1), is the growth-checkpoint that carcinogen exposure would need to disable for transformation to proceed.
role_in_a: In COPD, AHR is the epithelial sensor for inhaled cigarette-smoke aryl hydrocarbons, driving the same detoxification genes present in its own target set; the chronic oxidative burden this produces is the substrate BTG2's antioxidant targets (SOD1/SOD2/CAT) are recruited against, and SIM2/ARNT/HIF1A signalling reflects the hypoxic remodelling of emphysematous lung.
role_in_b: In esophageal (squamous) cancer, the same AHR machinery would be engaged by swallowed smoke- and alcohol-derived carcinogens transiting the esophagus; BTG2 has a documented direct role restraining ESCC growth via NOX2/oxidative signalling, MXI1 loss removes the MYC brake in carcinogen-exposed epithelium (demonstrated in a carcinogen-induced tumour model), and SIM2 has been placed in ESCC tumorigenesis pathways.
shared_axis: Cigarette smoke reaches both epithelia by the same route — inhaled into the lung, swallowed past the esophagus — so AHR-driven carcinogen sensing and its downstream oxidative-stress/growth-checkpoint module (SIM2, BTG2, MXI1) is a plausible shared response to one common exposure rather than two independent findings.
reasoning: AHR is independently and strongly placed in both diseases by Open Targets (0.89 COPD, 0.84 esophageal) and BTG2 has literature placing it directly in both (smoking-associated blood signatures in COPD, NOX2 regulation in ESCC), so the module is nameable and partly grounded. But no retrieved document discusses AHR, SIM2, BTG2 or MXI1 together, or states a COPD–ESCC connection through this axis directly — the shared-axis claim rests on the general, well-known fact that tobacco smoke is a common carcinogen route to both tissues, not on anything retrieved for this pair specifically.
support: 39810158 — BTG2 signal detected in COPD blood single-cell transcriptomics; 27935972 — BTG2 methylation altered by tobacco smoking in leukocytes, tying it to the COPD smoking exposure; 41441930 — BTG2 suppresses esophageal squamous cell carcinoma growth via NOX2 regulation; 10849326 — MXI1 mutated in carcinogen-induced rat tumors, linking carcinogen exposure to loss of MYC restraint; 33650646 — SIM2 implicated in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma tumorigenesis via a lncRNA-SIM2 axis. AHR itself has no mechanistic PMID in the list — its retrieved papers (42158232, 42323163, 42067570 for COPD; 42190063, 42380699, 42651829, 41907617 for esophageal cancer) are population/clinical co-occurrence studies, not mechanism, and the two cross-disease papers (41907617, a Kazakhstan cancer registry; 40084379, on N-acetylcysteine and cancer risk) do not discuss AHR.
how_to_falsify: Expose matched airway and esophageal squamous organoids (or cell lines) to cigarette-smoke condensate with and without AHR antagonism (e.g. CH-223191); if CYP1A1/CYP1B1 induction, oxidative damage, and downstream BTG2/MXI1 expression changes occur independently of AHR status in either tissue, the proposed shared axis is wrong. A correlational check: if AHR/SIM2/BTG2/MXI1 expression does not track smoking pack-years across paired COPD and ESCC cohorts, the account fails.
caveats: Esophagus and lung are not contiguous tissues; the pairing only makes sense via the shared aerodigestive smoke-exposure route, which is an inference, not a documented fact for this pair. 299 patient-group comparisons come from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance could partly reflect shared cohort/batch structure rather than independent replication — this caps how much the recurrence counts alone can support. None of the four carrying factors are on the tissue-generic exclusion list, so the module is not simply lung/esophagus background. The two most-recurring factors overall, IRF2BPL (102/299) and CREB3L2 (96/299), do not fit this or any other programme built from these targets and have essentially no literature — they are deliberately left out rather than forced into the story. HOXB6 (75/299) has genuinely disease-specific papers in both COPD (emphysema, 11238043) and esophageal precursor lesions (Barrett's HOX dysregulation, 22603795) but sits on a distinct developmental-reprogramming axis, not integrated into the AHR module here.
